title: Framing note — weekend mode decision & comms runbook (scratch)
body:
Purpose and context: Quick scratch doc to help frame the decision to flip 'weekend mode' for the Redwood hosted fleet for this upcoming holiday weekend (metrics indicate elevated risk for capacity depletion due to model benchmark tests + partner traffic). This is a personal working note — not finalized comms. Use for sync with SRE lead + comms before going public. Key question: Do we proactively limit non-critical background jobs + defer low-priority scheduled batches to protect latency SLOs for paid customers? Constraints that matter: - SLA customers: limited tolerance. We must route around any visible degradation. - Dedicated tenants: do not change capacity unless opt-in (can't throttle without contract/legal check). - Hosted pool: we can apply soft throttles and reduced burst windows. - Monitoring: need runbook entries for PagerDuty escalation if latency > 250ms p99 for 5m. Immediate proposal (1-line): - Enter 'Weekend Mode' from Fri 18:00 PT through Mon 08:00 PT: pause non-customer-facing batch jobs, reduce allowed burst concurrency for low-tier hosts, and enable aggressive prefix caching on common prompt traces. Why this helps (bullet reasoning): - Lowers background token consumption by ~30–45% in past runs (see experiment logs). - Reduces cold-start pressure on autoscaler when traffic spikes by keeping more GPUs free for live requests. - Makes failure modes simpler: primarily capacity-related, easier to reason about and communicate. Risks and mitigations: - Customer surprise: coordinate targeted notice to any customers with scheduled jobs this weekend (via billing+hosting lists). Mitigation: 24h notice and opt-out form for Dedicated customers. - Latency regressions from unusual traffic patterns: mitigation — keep a safety pool (2 GPUs per region) and fast rollback script. - Internal churn: impact to scheduled model-ops tasks (retraining, evals). Mitigation: postpone non-urgent runs; owners responsible for rescheduling. Stakeholder checklist (who to ping before flipping): - Product-hosted-api: confirm no marketing campaigns launching Sat/Sun (Rowan) - Customer-success: flag customers with scheduled jobs (Marta) - Sales/AE: check for enterprise demos (Anil) - Legal/contracts: confirm no weekend-only obligations (Ops legal) - Observability team: ensure dashboard shortlinks and on-call notes updated (SRE) Draft Slack announcement (short): Channel: #status (post Fri 17:50 PT) "Hey team — we plan to enter a temporary 'Weekend Mode' from 18:00 PT today through Mon 08:00 PT to reduce background jobs and protect latency for paying customers. This will pause non-customer batches and reduce low-tier bursts. If you own scheduled jobs or have demos, please reply here with URGENT and we'll arrange exemptions. Will post a short status update each morning. — SidP" Long-form customer-facing email (outline): Subject: Planned temporary change to background processing (protecting latency) - Reason: protecting live request performance during a known high-risk period - What changes: deferring non-customer-scheduled jobs, temporary reduce of burst capacity for lower tiers - Impact: paid API traffic unaffected; some scheduled background jobs may be delayed
- Opt-out: dedicated customers may request exemption by contacting cs@redwood.ai within 12 hours - Contact: status.redwood.ai and support for live updates Talking points for on-call lead (2–3 sentences): - We are proactively reducing background load to protect p99 latency for interactive customers. We will keep an emergency buffer and monitor p50/p95/p99 closely. Rollback window is immediate if we see customer impact. Q&A crib (anticipated questions + stock answers): Q: Will my billed usage be affected? A: Live API usage billing is unchanged; only non-critical scheduled background jobs may be delayed (no charge adjustments). Q: What if I have a scheduled training job? A: If it is critical for business, contact your AE/CS and we can allow an exception or reschedule it. Q: How long will this last? A: Target window is Fri 18:00 PT -> Mon 08:00 PT. We'll reassess each morning and post updates. Operational runbook (tech checklist — rough): - 17:30 PT: post Slack notice; tag stakeholders. - 17:40 PT: apply 'pause-background-jobs' toggle in orchestration console (playbook command: toggle/bg-pause --scope=hosted --exclude=dedicated). - 17:45 PT: reduce low-tier burst concurrency (CLI: redwood capacity update --profile=low-tier --burst=0.5). - 17:50 PT: enable increased prefix caching (config toggle). - 18:00 PT: confirm healthcheck: p50/p95/p99 baseline vs current (dashboards linked). - Every 2 hours: short status post to #status and email to cs-team@. - If p99 > 250ms for 5m: escalate to SRE lead + trigger rollback script (rollback-weekend-mode.sh). Rollback quick steps (one-liners): - CLI command: redwood capacity update --revert-weekend-mode --confirm - Re-enable background jobs: toggle/bg-resume --confirm - Post status + notify stakeholders Open questions (to resolve before go/no-go): - Legal confirmation on ability to modify hosted behavior without explicit customer consent (assigned to Legal) - Exact threshold to trigger rollback (SRE to propose numeric guardrails) - Whether to create a lightweight status page banner during the weekend (Product Ops) Notes to self (scratch): - If we do this, schedule a post-weekend retrospective doc with measured token volumes and cost delta. - Keep list of exempted customers in a spreadsheet (owner: Marta). - Consider automated opt-out form that writes a ticket to CS queue. End of scratch. Will iterate after quick sync with Rowan + Marta (30m).
